title: Anthropic's AI Infrastructure Commitments Now Reach $895B to Outpace Meta

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock
Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Anthropic has designated approximately $70 billion for AI infrastructure payments over the next 12 months, according to updated registration statements for the company's initial public offering. The AI developer has allocated $161 billion to Broadcom for chip leases and hardware, $121 billion to Google, and at least $110 billion to Amazon to secure computing power and data center access. The company also pledged $121 billion to SpaceX, and officials estimate that total obligations could exceed $1 trillion if additional unpriced agreements are finalized.

The AI firm's total future commitments reach $895.4 billion, a sum that now exceeds the $866 billion in pledges made by Meta and trails only Alphabet's $1.06 trillion. Of that amount, $448 billion will be spent by 2030, including more than $313 billion in purchases that are largely non-cancelable. These spending targets coincide with a reduction in technical goals, as the company now expects to have 3.5 GW of compute capacity by the end of 2026, down from the 5 GW target it provided to investors in September.

selectedTweets.text:
The NYT reported on Nov 3 that Anthropic expects to have +3.5 gigawatts of computing capacity by the end of this year and aims to 2x that figure next year (~7GW+). 

As recently as September NYT piece said the company told investors that it plans to have ~5 GW worth of compute available to use by the end of the year, with about 10 GW for 2027. 

=Year-end and 2027 targets are both down roughly 30%(!) in ~2 months if you believe this NYT report. 

Anthropic is THE company at the heart of the AI buildout and if they are having trouble getting more capacity online, you have to imagine the rest of the industry will be challenged. Don't underestimate the difficulty of bringing on GWs of compute. 

To be clear, it's one media report, among many. Anthropic has many partners. Some may accelerate/decelerate based on specific factors. But, in general, it's something worth paying attention to if it ends up being real. We have many aggressive GW add forecasts out there.

It does boost monetization math, though. On 3.5GW, 25% inference = ~900MW. At $75BN run-rate that's ~$21B rev/total GW and ~$86B rev/inference GW. At $100B that's ~$29BN rev/total GW and ~$114B/inference GW.

selectedTweets.text:
was reading anthropic's s-1: 
h1 2026 capex was just $482M. 
signed leases that haven't even started yet: ~$321B

they own almost none of their compute. landlords, power companies and chip vendors carry the assets 

1. purchase commitments went from ~$55B to ~$266B in six months

2. some power deals run 20 years with uncapped fuel pass-through. whoever builds those plants is underwriting anthropic's credit for two decades

3. broadcom had to guarantee lenders on the $63B chip lease (up to ~$43B) to get it financed. the chip vendor is now on the hook if anthropic stops paying

the memory angle? samsung and sk hynix just signed long-term supply deals and want 50 to 80% of capacity locked in, citing shortages into 2028-30. commitments like anthropic's are the demand those contracts are written against. so memory makers have the same exposure as the landlords, just one step further back

compute fell to 55% of revenue in h1, from 160% in 2025. the number i'd track every quarter is that ratio. if it turns back up, a lot of suppliers find out how exposed they are

(h/t Global Data Center Hub for the s-1 breakdown)

selectedTweets.text:
Anthropic has now disclosed a record $895 billion in future AI infrastructure spending commitments.

This includes both purchase commitments and leases for computing power and related infrastructure.

$448 billion, or 50%, is expected to be incurred by the end of 2030, with ~$70 billion due over the next 12 months.

The biggest commitments are to Broadcom, $AVGO, at $161 billion, followed by Google at $121 billion, with up to $150 billion in additional estimated spending on Google's AI chips.

Anthropic has also committed up to $121 billion to SpaceX, $SPCX, and at least $110 billion to Amazon, $AMZN.

For perspective, among Big Tech companies, only Alphabet, $GOOGL, has larger commitments, at $1.06 trillion, while Meta, $META, follows with $866 billion.

The scale of Anthropic's spending obligations is unprecedented.
